title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: A trade union bilateral agreement between Cambodia Labour Confederation (CLC) and Fisher Rights Network (FRN) Thailand was signed for the better protection of migrant fishers on 31 March 2023. The agreement aims to increase trade union membership both in Thailand and Cambodia, provide legal assistance to Cambodian migrant workers, conduct informal pre-departure orientation at origin communities, and organize regular updates to address issues concerning migrant workers. The ILO, with support from the European Union (EU), provided technical guidance on the development of the trade union bilateral agreement between Cambodia and Thailand. The ILO coordinated two exchange visits between the trade unions to better understand the situation of migrant workers in both countries on 4-6 Oct and 27-30 Nov 2022.

title.narrative: 7.5.3. Number of bilateral or regional labour migration frameworks, with monitoring and review mechanisms to protect the labour rights of migrant workers
Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: From 2022-2023, Migrant Worker Resource Centers (MRCs) run by the Provincial Department of Labour and Vocational Training (PDoLVT), the National Employment Agency (NEA), the Cambodian Labour Confederation, and CSOs (Gender and Development Cambodia or GADC, Legal Services for Children and Women, Cambodian Women’s Crisis Center, Phnom Srey Organization for Development or PSOD, and the Center for Alliance of Labour and Human Rights) improved access of around 23,604 Cambodian migrant workers and their families (M: 8,213; W: 15,391)) to justice, migration counselling, information and education, networking and union organization/membership. MoLVT TVET provided skills training and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) to 80 trainees (M: 40, W: 40) by June 2023. NEA, together with PDoLVTs rolled out the SaverAsia web platform and app, empowering migrant workers to achieve financial goals by comparing remittance rates, using a budget calculator, and learning to manage and transfer money. From January 2022 until now, the Khmer language SaverAsia Cambodia platform reached 2.97 million people. GADC and PSOD established 5 new migrant women groups with 109 members in Prey Veng and Kampong Cham which are starting to lobby for non-discriminatory principles, reintegration support services, and GBV prevention and response. The Association of Cambodian Recruitment Agencies (ACRA) and the Manpower Association of Cambodia (MAC) developed and adopted an assessment framework and checklist of the Code of Conduct (CoC) for Cambodian recruitment agencies in 2022. The associations signed the Cambodia CoC for Private Recruitment Agencies and Launched the COC Assessment System Pilot on 12 December 2022. ILO, with support from the Government of Australia and the EU, provided technical assistance and training for MRC staff and other key actors, through: -Training for service providers to improve dispute resolution services for migrant workers in fishing and seafood processing. - Dispute resolution training to 94 participants in Pursat, Banteay Meanchey, - MRC Operations training to 216 participants on migration and labour rights, violence and harassment, - Training on migration regulations, fair recruitment and gender-responsive services to 186 local leaders, - Training of 18 service providers on financial literacy training for migrant workers, especially women. - Cross-border dialogue for 30 recruitment agency representatives in Cambodia, Thailand, Malaysia on violence and harassment. ILO, with support from the Governments of Australia, New Zealand, and Switzerland, provided technical support on Skills training and RPL services for migrants with PDoLVT Battambang, the Battambang Institute of Technology (BIT), École d’Hôtellerie et de Tourisme Paul Dubrule (EHT), National Polytechnic Institute of Angkor (NPIA), and National Polytechnic Institute of Cambodia (NPIC). ILO, with support from the Governments of Australia and Canada, supported the rollout of SaverAsia Cambodia by developing Khmer language social media and collaborated with NEA and PDoLVTs for in-person outreach and training events in high outmigration areas. ILO, with support from the Governments of Australia and Canada, collaborated with new migrant women's groups for technical training on women’s empowerment, and group leadership and formation. ILO, with support from the Government of Australia, assisted two private recruitment agency associations in developing their Code of Conduct assessment framework, checklist and organized a high-level Signing Ceremony.

description.narrative:
The 2023 – 2025 National Action Plan to implement the 2017 ASEAN Consensus on the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of Migrant Workers (NAP) was endorsed by the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training (MOLVT). Cambodia is the first ASEAN Member State to develop a NAP to implement the 2017 ASEAN Consensus. Cambodia developed a National Implementation Plan (NIP) for the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM). ILO, with support from the Government of Australia, provided technical inputs on a draft National Action Plan following the joint hosting of a tripartite-plus consultation to collect inputs from stakeholders.
ILO, with support from the Government of Australia, worked with the UN Network on Migration, the Government, the private sector and key stakeholders in Cambodia, and provided technical support to the development of the NIP GCM, ensuring the policy reflects rights-based and gender-responsive planning.
